items.title: Anonymous visitor sees a log-in prompt instead of received messages and tokens
covers: Expected: step 2 shows no received message and no token
Expected: the messages section asks the visitor to log in, as the registered webhooks section does
Actual: step 2 lists the received message with its data and its token
items.reason: This is the bug itself: a visitor who is not signed in could read every received webhook message and its token. It reproduces the ticket's exact steps (deliver a message, open the home page in a fresh, signed-out browser context) and fails if any message data or token reaches the page. It must be e2e because the leak is what an unauthenticated browser sees on the Blazor page; a fresh context stands in for the private window.

items.title: Signed-in user sees received messages with When, Data and Token as before
covers: Expected: signed in, the webhook client shows the received messages exactly as today
items.reason: The fix gates the messages list behind sign-in; this guards the other half of the contract, that a signed-in user still sees each received message with its When, Data and Token exactly as before. Without it, a fix that hid the list from everyone would pass TC-BUG-50-01. It must be e2e because it needs a real OIDC sign-in through Identity on the test stack.
